name: Memorial sites of the Genocide: Nyamata, Murambi, Gisozi and Bisesero
subtitle: A cultural property on the UNESCO World Heritage List since 2023.

parts.text: UNESCO describes the property in these words: “Between April and July 1994, an estimated one million people were killed across Rwanda by armed militias called Interahamwe that targeted Tutsi, but also executed moderate Hutu and Twa people. The victims of the genocide are commemorated in this serial property composed of four memorial sites. Two of the component parts were scenes of massacres: a Catholic church built in the hill of Nyamata in 1980, and a technical school built in the hill of Murambi in 1990. The hill of Gisozi in Kigali City hosts the Kigali Genocide Memorial built in 1999, where more than 250,000 victims have been buried, while the hill of Bisesero in the Western Province hosts a memorial built in 1998, to remember the fight of those who resisted their perpetrators for over two months before being exterminated.”
The property includes four memorial sites. Only one of them, Gisozi, is the Kigali Genocide Memorial, which this card draws on; Nyamata, Murambi and Bisesero are not covered here.

Wikipedia says the Gisozi memorial commemorates the 1994 genocide against the Tutsi and holds the remains of over 250,000 people. It is run by the Aegis Trust on behalf of the National Commission for the Fight Against Genocide.
The article says that precisely how many people were killed may never be known, that estimates vary from 500,000 to over a million, and that a figure close to 800,000 is widely accepted.

gaps: The other three sites, and survivors' own accounts: the right voices here are those of survivors and Rwandan historians, and this card has none of them yet.
The wording of the numbers and of the genocide's history should be checked with Rwandan institutions before publication.
